# Roadmap — the rest of the module {#sec-roadmap}

This booklet grows by teaching day. Six are written; the ones below that are
not are the obvious continuations, each with the loose end it picks up.
@sec-add-a-day explains how to add one.

| Day | Title | Picks up from | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | From code to a model that might be wrong | — | written |
| 2 | Seeing the data, and not leaking it | the data was handed to us clean (1.2) | written |
| 3 | Fitting a line, and why it fits | `lm()` was a black box (1.2) | written |
| 4 | Predicting a class, and choosing a threshold | a decision is not a prediction | written |
| 5 | Measuring performance, and trees that overfit | MAE was chosen for us (1.4) | written |

| 9 | Reporting a model | the one-sentence claim (1.4), TRIPOD+AI | to write |

: {tbl-colwidths="[6,36,40,18]"}

Days 2 to 6 were built from the module's earlier standalone sites, and the
conversion changed three things on purpose: both languages now read the same
file, every reported number is produced by code in the chapter rather than
quoted from an earlier run, and each exercise carries a control. Each day's
`dayN-CHANGES.md`, kept out of the published booklet, records what differs from
the original pages.

## Principles the later days should keep

These are what make the booklet a course rather than a pile of notebooks.

1. **Every exercise carries a control.** A student who has only run a pipeline
   believes its output. One who has watched the same pipeline survive — or fail
   — a baseline, a shuffled label, or a no-shift extract believes the *method*.
   Day 1 has three controls: the predict-the-mean baseline, extract A, and the
   refitted-coefficient comparison.
2. **Nothing is introduced before the object it acts on.** Cross-validation is
   only meaningful once a student has felt a single split wobble.
3. **Each exercise ends with what cannot be claimed.** The limitation is not a
   disclaimer; it is the hook for the next day.
4. **Both languages, every time.** Where they genuinely differ, say so and say
   why, rather than presenting one as a translation of the other.
5. **The provenance of every dataset is written down.** Day 1's data is
   simulated and its generating process is published, which is the only way a
   student can discover that their diagnosis was wrong. Days 2 to 6 use a
   synthetic diabetes dataset and two small clinical teaching files, documented
   in @sec-data — including why the dataset the exercises were originally
   written against is no longer used.
6. **Every day fits on twenty printed pages.** The site carries the discussion;
   the worksheet carries the tasks. If a day will not fit, the narrative moves
   into a `::: {.web-only}` block rather than the tasks being cut.
